title: Per-route fidelity budgeting and adaptive quant tuner
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an automated, per-route quantization tuning pipeline that assigns a fidelity budget to each API route and uses adaptive perturbation schedules to find safe int8/int4 (AWQ/GPTQ) profiles. The tuner should balance token-cost savings against per-route quality SLOs (latency and semantic quality) and produce deployment gates and rollback thresholds usable by Console rollouts.
background: We have observed that a single global quant threshold is suboptimal: chat endpoints, short-completion routes, and reranking calls show different sensitivity to bitwidth changes and AWQ vs GPTQ trade-offs. Current evals run broad cohort sweeps but lack per-route budgets and an automated annealing process that accounts for production token distributions and SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Per-route fidelity budget defined and stored in config (JSON blob) with human-readable rationale
Adaptive tuner can run a perturbation schedule for a route and return a ranked list of candidate quant profiles with expected quality delta and token-savings estimate
Generated candidates include fallback profiles and an automatic rollback threshold (delta metric) per route
Integration with Console rollouts: can pass candidate profiles to a canary rollout API with gating rules and automatic rollback on breach
End-to-end smoke test demonstrating safe deploy of an int4 AWQ profile on a low-risk route with verified semantic delta < configured threshold
implementation_notes: Tuner core: Bayesian bandit + simulated annealing hybrid that explores int4/int8 combos and AWQ/GPTQ knobs (per-layer grouping)

Inputs: route id, historical token-length distribution, exemplar prompt set (up to 500), quality metric(s) selection (e.g., semantic-similarity, BLEU, edit-distance), SLO budget (semantic delta allowed)
Evaluation harness: streaming evals against production-like traffic replay and synthetic perturbations (typos, prompts with trailing system tokens, multi-turn contexts)
Cost model: token savings estimator using batching/caching config and per-model throughput profile
Profile representation: compact profile string plus metadata (bitwidth map, per-layer clamp flags, quant library selector AWQ|GPTQ)
Output: artifact (S3 path) and rollup JSON with metrics: median semantic delta, 95p latency delta, token-saved-per-1M-reqs
Rollback decision: threshold is computed using bootstrap confidence intervals (default: 95% CI) and a safety margin of +10% on measured delta
test_plan: Unit tests for tuner heuristics and cost-model components
Deterministic integration test that runs tuner on a synthetic route and validates candidate ordering stability
Regression harness: run candidate profiles against existing quant-regression smoke suite (int4/int8) and ensure no silent semantic regressions on golden prompts
Production shadow run for 2 weeks on <5% traffic for selected low-risk route; automatically collect metrics and compare to baseline
Canary rollout test: validate automatic rollback triggers on injected semantic regressions using OSS perturbation scripts
metrics: Quality: mean semantic-similarity delta (ROUGE/BERTScore) per route
Reliability: % of runs where rollback was triggered within configured window
Economics: estimated tokens saved per million requests and realized cost delta
Latency: median and 95th-percentile latency delta after profile applied
rollout_plan: Phase 1: bench-only offline runs (1 week). Phase 2: shadow deploy to capture real traffic signals (2 weeks). Phase 3: canary rollout to 1% of traffic with auto-rollback enabled. Phase 4: progressive ramp to 25% then 100% after manual sign-off.
risks: Overfitting tuner to synthetic exemplars that don't reflect long-tail production prompts
False negatives in semantic regression detection for some languages and low-resource cohorts
AWQ vs GPTQ behavior variance across models leading to noisy candidate scores
Cost-model inaccuracies may overestimate savings leading to poor economic decisions
mitigations: Require production prompt sampling and minimum 48h shadow-run data before approving a candidate
Maintain per-locale evaluation sets and add cross-lingual distance checks
Aggregate multiple quality metrics (semantic + token-level) and use ensemble scoring
Conservative default safety margin on rollback thresholds and manual sign-off for high-impact routes
